subproblem.title: Lusin exhaustion: a Borel map into a finite-dimensional normed space is continuous on countably many compact sets exhausting a finite-measure Borel set up to a null set (parent Step 3, Lusin part)
subproblem.statement: Let Y be a finite-dimensional real normed space (a type in universe Type) equipped with its Borel σ-algebra, let n ∈ ℕ, let ℝⁿ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) carry Lebesgue measure Lⁿ = volume, let g: ℝⁿ → Y be Borel measurable, and let S ⊆ ℝⁿ be a Borel set with Lⁿ(S) < ∞. Then there are compact sets C_j ⊆ S (j ∈ ℕ) such that g is continuous on each C_j and Lⁿ(S ∖ ⋃_j C_j) = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ {Y : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup Y] [NormedSpace ℝ Y] [FiniteDimensional ℝ Y] [MeasurableSpace Y] [BorelSpace Y] (n : ℕ) (g : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → Y) (S : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))), Measurable g → MeasurableSet S → volume S ≠ ⊤ → ∃ C : ℕ → Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)), (∀ j, IsCompact (C j) ∧ C j ⊆ S ∧ ContinuousOn g (C j)) ∧ volume (S \ ⋃ j, C j) = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝⁿ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with Lebesgue measure Lⁿ := volume; Y is a finite-dimensional real normed space with its Borel σ-algebra; g: ℝⁿ → Y is Borel measurable; S ⊆ ℝⁿ is Borel with Lⁿ(S) < ∞. This is the Lusin part of Step 3 of the parent proof, stated for an arbitrary finite-dimensional target; for Y = L(ℝⁿ, ℝ^{n+ℓ}) and orthonormal bases (e_a), (e'_b) the coordinates in step 1 may be taken to be the matrix entries ⟨g(w)e_a, e'_b⟩ used there.

1. (Coordinates.) Let d := dim Y and fix a basis b_1, …, b_d of Y (Mathlib Module.finBasis ℝ Y). Because Y is finite-dimensional, the coordinate map Φ: Y → ℝ^d, determined by y = Σ_i Φ(y)_i·b_i, is a continuous linear equivalence, i.e. Φ and Φ⁻¹ are continuous (Basis.equivFunL). For i ∈ {1, …, d} let g_i: ℝⁿ → ℝ, g_i(w) := Φ(g(w))_i. Each g_i is Borel measurable, as the composition of the continuous (hence Borel) map y ↦ Φ(y)_i with the Borel map g.

2. (Regularity of Lⁿ.) Lⁿ is weakly regular, so for every Borel A ⊆ ℝⁿ with Lⁿ(A) < ∞ and every δ > 0 there is a closed F ⊆ A with Lⁿ(A ∖ F) < δ (Mathlib MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_sdiff_lt). Lⁿ is also inner regular by compact sets on sets of finite measure: for such A and δ there is a compact K ⊆ A with Lⁿ(A ∖ K) < δ (MeasurableSet.exists_isCompact_sdiff_lt).

3. (One compact set.) Let ε > 0 be real and put δ := ε/(2(d + 1)) > 0.
 (a) For each i ∈ {1, …, d}, Lusin's theorem for real-valued functions (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17; Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable in module Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.Lusin, which the proof file must import), applied with ν := Lⁿ, with its regularity hypothesis supplied by the first part of step 2, with A := S, f := g_i and tolerance δ, gives a closed set D_i ⊆ S with Lⁿ(S ∖ D_i) < δ such that g_i is continuous on D_i.
 (b) By the second part of step 2 there is a compact K ⊆ S with Lⁿ(S ∖ K) < ε/2.
 (c) Put C := K ∩ ⋂_{i=1}^{d} D_i (so C = K when d = 0). C is compact, being the intersection of the compact set K with the closed set ⋂_i D_i (IsCompact.inter_right, isClosed_iInter), and C ⊆ K ⊆ S.
 (d) If x ∈ S ∖ C, then x ∉ K or x ∉ D_i for some i; hence S ∖ C ⊆ (S ∖ K) ∪ ⋃_{i=1}^{d} (S ∖ D_i). By monotonicity and finite subadditivity,
   Lⁿ(S ∖ C) ≤ Lⁿ(S ∖ K) + Σ_{i=1}^{d} Lⁿ(S ∖ D_i) < ε/2 + d·δ ≤ ε/2 + (d + 1)·δ = ε/2 + ε/2 = ε,
 where the strict inequality uses Lⁿ(S ∖ K) < ε/2, Lⁿ(S ∖ D_i) ≤ δ and the finiteness of d·δ.
 (e) For each i, g_i is continuous on D_i ⊇ C, hence on C. A map into the finite product ℝ^d is continuous on C iff all its components are (continuousOn_pi), so w ↦ Φ(g(w)) = (g_1(w), …, g_d(w)) is continuous on C; therefore g = Φ⁻¹ ∘ (Φ ∘ g) is continuous on C, Φ⁻¹ being continuous.

4. (Exhaustion.) For every j ∈ ℕ apply step 3 with ε := 1/(j + 1) and call the resulting set C_j. Then C_j is compact, C_j ⊆ S, g is continuous on C_j and Lⁿ(S ∖ C_j) < 1/(j + 1). For every j we have S ∖ ⋃_i C_i ⊆ S ∖ C_j, so Lⁿ(S ∖ ⋃_i C_i) ≤ 1/(j + 1). Given η > 0 there is j with 1/(j + 1) < η (ENNReal.exists_inv_nat_lt), so Lⁿ(S ∖ ⋃_i C_i) ≤ η for every η > 0, i.e. Lⁿ(S ∖ ⋃_i C_i) = 0. Thus the sequence (C_j)_{j∈ℕ} consists of compact subsets of S on each of which g is continuous, and it exhausts S up to an Lⁿ-null set, as asserted.
proof_key_steps: Fix a basis of Y: the coordinate map Φ: Y → ℝ^d is a continuous linear equivalence (Basis.equivFunL) and each coordinate g_i = Φ(·)_i ∘ g is Borel
Lⁿ is weakly regular (closed inner approximation, the regularity hypothesis of SimonGMT's Lusin theorem) and inner regular by compact sets on Borel sets of finite measure

For ε > 0: Lusin for each g_i gives closed D_i ⊆ S with Lⁿ(S ∖ D_i) < ε/(2(d+1)), inner regularity gives compact K ⊆ S with Lⁿ(S ∖ K) < ε/2; C := K ∩ ⋂_i D_i is compact, C ⊆ S, Lⁿ(S ∖ C) < ε, and g = Φ⁻¹ ∘ (g_1, …, g_d) is continuous on C
Taking ε = 1/(j+1) gives C_j; Lⁿ(S ∖ ⋃_i C_i) ≤ 1/(j+1) for every j, hence Lⁿ(S ∖ ⋃_i C_i) = 0

audit.reason: The proposition includes every stated space, measurability and finite-measure hypothesis; volume S ≠ ⊤ expresses the stated finiteness. Basis coordinates permit the cited real-valued Lusin theorem, compact inner approximation supplies compactness, and the finite error estimate is valid, including d = 0 because its denominator uses d + 1. Continuity reconstructs through the inverse coordinate equivalence, and the reciprocal error bounds force a null remainder. No missing construction or circular reliance remains.

subproblem.title: Regular points of a continuous map lie in countably many bounded Borel sets with a uniform lower Lipschitz bound (parent Steps 1–2)
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, ℝⁿ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), E := Ambient n ℓ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n+ℓ)), and let f: ℝⁿ → E be continuous. Let R := {w ∈ ℝⁿ : f is (Fréchet) differentiable at w and its derivative Df(w) = fderiv ℝ f w is injective}. Then there are sets T_p ⊆ ℝⁿ (p ∈ ℕ) with R ⊆ ⋃_p T_p such that, for every p: T_p is a Borel set; T_p is bounded; at every w ∈ T_p the map f is differentiable and Df(w) is injective (i.e. T_p ⊆ R); and there is c > 0 with c|v − w| ≤ |f(v) − f(w)| for all v, w ∈ T_p.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → Ambient n ℓ), Continuous f → ∃ T : ℕ → Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)), {w | DifferentiableAt ℝ f w ∧ Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ f w)} ⊆ ⋃ p, T p ∧ ∀ p, MeasurableSet (T p) ∧ Bornology.IsBounded (T p) ∧ (∀ w ∈ T p, DifferentiableAt ℝ f w ∧ Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ f w)) ∧ ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ v ∈ T p, ∀ w ∈ T p, c * ‖v - w‖ ≤ ‖f v - f w‖
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝⁿ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) and E := Ambient n ℓ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n+ℓ)) carry their Euclidean norms |·| and Borel σ-algebras; B_ρ(q) := {x : |x − q| ≤ ρ} is the closed ball; Df(w) := fderiv ℝ f w. Let R := {w ∈ ℝⁿ : f is differentiable at w and Df(w) is injective}. For k ∈ ℕ put r_k := 1/(k+1) ∈ (0, 1] and
  G_k := ⋂_{u ∈ ℝⁿ, |u| ≤ r_k} {w ∈ ℝⁿ : r_k·|u| ≤ |f(w + u) − f(w)|},   S_k := R ∩ G_k.
(This is Step 1 of the parent proof, with the integer k+1 ≥ 1 in place of k.)

1. (R is Borel.) R is exactly SimonGMT's Chapter02.areaRegularSet f = {x | DifferentiableAt ℝ f x ∧ Injective (fderiv ℝ f x)}, which is Borel by Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.measurableSet_areaRegularSet (module Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaLipschitz of the pinned SimonGMT package, axioms propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound; the proof file must import this module). [Its content: {w : f is differentiable at w} is Borel (Mathlib measurableSet_of_differentiableAt), and on this set injectivity of Df(w) is equivalent to the non-vanishing of the Borel function w ↦ Jf(w) = det(Df(w)*Df(w))^{1/2}.]

2. (G_k is closed, S_k is Borel.) Fix k and u ∈ ℝⁿ. The function w ↦ |f(w + u) − f(w)| is continuous, because f is continuous and translation, subtraction and the norm are continuous; hence {w : r_k·|u| ≤ |f(w + u) − f(w)|} is closed (Mathlib isClosed_le). An intersection of closed sets is closed (isClosed_biInter), so G_k is closed, hence Borel, and S_k = R ∩ G_k is Borel by step 1.

3. (Lower bound for an injective linear map.) Let L: ℝⁿ → E be linear and injective. Since ℝⁿ is finite-dimensional and ker L = {0}, L is anti-Lipschitz: there is K > 0 with |u| ≤ K·|Lu| for all u ∈ ℝⁿ (Mathlib LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith applied to L with LinearMap.ker_eq_bot, then ZeroHomClass.bound_of_antilipschitz). [Directly: if n = 0 then every u is 0 and any K works; if n ≥ 1, the continuous function e ↦ |Le| is positive on the compact nonempty unit sphere, so it has a minimum μ > 0, and K := 1/μ works by homogeneity.] Put m := 1/K > 0; then |Lu| ≥ m·|u| for all u ∈ ℝⁿ.

4. (R = ⋃_k S_k.) Clearly S_k ⊆ R for every k. Conversely, let w ∈ R, put L := Df(w), and let m > 0 be given by step 3 for L. Since f has derivative L at w, f(w + u) − f(w) − Lu = o(|u|) as u → 0 (Mathlib hasFDerivAt_iff_isLittleO_nhds_zero); applying the definition of o(·) with the constant m/2 > 0 (Asymptotics.IsLittleO.def, Metric.eventually_nhds_iff) gives r > 0 such that |f(w + u) − f(w) − Lu| ≤ (m/2)·|u| for every u with |u| < r. For such u the triangle inequality gives
  |f(w + u) − f(w)| ≥ |Lu| − |f(w + u) − f(w) − Lu| ≥ m·|u| − (m/2)·|u| = (m/2)·|u|.
By the Archimedean property choose k ∈ ℕ with k + 1 > max(2/m, 2/r). Then r_k = 1/(k+1) < r/2 < r and r_k < m/2. Let u ∈ ℝⁿ with |u| ≤ r_k. Then |u| < r, so |f(w + u) − f(w)| ≥ (m/2)·|u| ≥ r_k·|u|. Hence w ∈ G_k, and since w ∈ R, w ∈ S_k.

5. (Small balls.) ℝⁿ is separable and nonempty (it contains 0), so there is a sequence (q_m)_{m∈ℕ} in ℝⁿ with dense range (Mathlib TopologicalSpace.exists_dense_seq; e.g. an enumeration of the points with rational coordinates). For k, m ∈ ℕ put Q_{k,m} := B_{r_k/2}(q_m). For each fixed k the balls Q_{k,m}, m ∈ ℕ, cover ℝⁿ: given w ∈ ℝⁿ, density gives m with |w − q_m| < r_k/2 (DenseRange.exists_dist_lt), so w ∈ Q_{k,m}.

6. (The family.) Let p ↦ (k(p), m(p)) := Nat.unpair p, a bijection ℕ → ℕ × ℕ whose inverse is (k, m) ↦ Nat.pair k m (Nat.unpair_pair). For p ∈ ℕ define
  T_p := S_{k(p)} ∩ Q_{k(p), m(p)} = R ∩ G_{k(p)} ∩ B_{r_{k(p)}/2}(q_{m(p)}).

7. (Covering.) Let w ∈ R. By step 4 there is k with w ∈ S_k, and by step 5 there is m with w ∈ Q_{k,m}. For p := Nat.pair k m we have (k(p), m(p)) = (k, m), hence w ∈ T_p. Thus R ⊆ ⋃_p T_p.

8. (Properties of each T_p.) Fix p and write k := k(p), m := m(p).
 (a) T_p is Borel, as the intersection of the Borel set S_k (step 2) with the closed ball Q_{k,m}.
 (b) T_p is bounded, being contained in the ball Q_{k,m}.
 (c) T_p ⊆ S_k ⊆ R, i.e. at every w ∈ T_p the map f is differentiable and Df(w) is injective.
 (d) Put c := r_k = 1/(k+1) > 0. Let v, w ∈ T_p. Then |v − w| ≤ |v − q_m| + |w − q_m| ≤ r_k/2 + r_k/2 = r_k. Let u := v − w, so |u| ≤ r_k and w + u = v. Since w ∈ G_k, the defining inequality of G_k for this u gives r_k·|u| ≤ |f(w + u) − f(w)|, that is, c·|v − w| ≤ |f(v) − f(w)|.
Steps 7 and 8 are exactly the assertions of the theorem: R ⊆ ⋃_p T_p, and every T_p is Borel, bounded, contained in R and carries the lower bound with the constant c = 1/(k(p)+1) > 0.
proof_key_steps: R is Borel (SimonGMT Chapter02.measurableSet_areaRegularSet) and G_k := ⋂_{|u| ≤ 1/(k+1)} {w : |u|/(k+1) ≤ |f(w+u) − f(w)|} is closed because f is continuous, so S_k := R ∩ G_k is Borel
An injective linear L: ℝⁿ → E satisfies |Lu| ≥ m|u| for some m > 0 (finite-dimensional anti-Lipschitz bound, LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith)
At w ∈ R, differentiability gives r > 0 with |f(w+u) − f(w)| ≥ (m/2)|u| for |u| < r; choosing k + 1 > max(2/m, 2/r) gives w ∈ S_k, so R = ⋃_k S_k
With a dense sequence (q_m), the sets T_p := S_k ∩ B_{1/(2(k+1))}(q_m), (k, m) = Nat.unpair p, cover R
Each T_p is Borel, bounded and contained in R, and for v, w ∈ T_p one has |v − w| ≤ 1/(k+1), so u := v − w in the definition of G_k gives (1/(k+1))|v − w| ≤ |f(v) − f(w)|

audit.reason: The one-line proposition exactly matches the prose, including continuity and unrestricted natural dimensions. Every proof step is justified: the regular set is Borel, the uniform-increment sets are closed, injectivity gives a positive linear lower bound even when n = 0, differentiability supplies a sufficiently small radius, and dense-sequence balls give the bounded countable cover and pairwise lower bound. This is an independent, non-circular analytic obligation.

subproblem.title: The image of one Lipschitz map ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+ℓ} is covered, up to an Hⁿ-null set, by compact bi-Lipschitz pieces with continuous injective derivative (parent Steps 3–5)
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, ℝⁿ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), E := Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, Hⁿ := μHE[n] the n-dimensional (Euclidean-normalized) Hausdorff measure on E, K ≥ 0, and let f: ℝⁿ → E be K-Lipschitz. Then there are a set Y ⊆ E with Hⁿ(Y) = 0 and sets C_i ⊆ ℝⁿ (i ∈ ℕ) with f(ℝⁿ) ⊆ Y ∪ ⋃_i f(C_i) such that, for every i: C_i is compact; f is differentiable at every w ∈ C_i and Df(w) is injective; w ↦ Df(w) = fderiv ℝ f w is continuous on C_i; and there is c > 0 with c|v − w| ≤ |f(v) − f(w)| for all v, w ∈ C_i.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (K : NNReal) (f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → Ambient n ℓ), LipschitzWith K f → ∃ (Y : Set (Ambient n ℓ)) (C : ℕ → Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))), (μHE[n] : Measure (Ambient n ℓ)) Y = 0 ∧ Set.range f ⊆ Y ∪ ⋃ i, f '' C i ∧ ∀ i, IsCompact (C i) ∧ (∀ w ∈ C i, DifferentiableAt ℝ f w ∧ Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ f w)) ∧ ContinuousOn (fderiv ℝ f) (C i) ∧ ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ v ∈ C i, ∀ w ∈ C i, c * ‖v - w‖ ≤ ‖f v - f w‖
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝⁿ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with Lebesgue measure Lⁿ := volume; E := Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ}; Hⁿ := μHE[n] (on E, and on ℝⁿ where it equals Lⁿ); Df(w) := fderiv ℝ f w; R := {w ∈ ℝⁿ : f is differentiable at w and Df(w) is injective}; f is K-Lipschitz. This is Steps 3–5 of the parent proof for one map f. It uses the sibling theorems regular_set_lower_lipschitz_cover (Steps 1–2 of the parent proof) and lusin_compact_exhaustion_of_measurable (the Lusin part of Step 3).

1. (Bi-Lipschitz Borel pieces of R.) f is Lipschitz, hence continuous. By the sibling theorem regular_set_lower_lipschitz_cover applied to f there are sets T_p ⊆ ℝⁿ (p ∈ ℕ) with R ⊆ ⋃_p T_p such that, for every p, T_p is Borel, T_p is bounded, T_p ⊆ R, and there is a constant c_p > 0 with c_p·|v − w| ≤ |f(v) − f(w)| for all v, w ∈ T_p; fix such a c_p for every p.

2. (Finite measure.) Each T_p is bounded, so its closure is compact (Heine–Borel) and Lⁿ(T_p) ≤ Lⁿ(closure T_p) < ∞, Lⁿ being finite on compact sets (Mathlib Bornology.IsBounded.measure_lt_top).

3. (Compact pieces with continuous derivative.) The map g := fderiv ℝ f: ℝⁿ → L(ℝⁿ, E) (equal to Df(w) where f is differentiable and to 0 elsewhere) is Borel measurable (Mathlib measurable_fderiv), and L(ℝⁿ, E) with the operator norm is a finite-dimensional real normed space carrying its Borel σ-algebra. For every p, the sibling theorem lusin_compact_exhaustion_of_measurable applied to g and S := T_p (Borel, with Lⁿ(T_p) < ∞ by step 2) gives compact sets D_{p,q} ⊆ T_p (q ∈ ℕ) such that g is continuous on every D_{p,q} and Lⁿ(T_p ∖ ⋃_q D_{p,q}) = 0.

4. (The pieces.) Let i ↦ (p(i), q(i)) := Nat.unpair i, a bijection ℕ → ℕ × ℕ whose inverse is (p, q) ↦ Nat.pair p q, and put C_i := D_{p(i), q(i)}. Fix i. Then C_i is compact (step 3). Since C_i ⊆ T_{p(i)} ⊆ R, f is differentiable at every w ∈ C_i and Df(w) is injective. The map w ↦ Df(w) = fderiv ℝ f w is continuous on C_i (step 3). Finally c := c_{p(i)} > 0 satisfies c·|v − w| ≤ |f(v) − f(w)| for all v, w ∈ C_i, because C_i ⊆ T_{p(i)} (step 1).

5. (The exceptional set.) Let Z := ⋃_{p∈ℕ} (T_p ∖ ⋃_q D_{p,q}) ⊆ ℝⁿ and Y := f(ℝⁿ ∖ R) ∪ f(Z) ⊆ E.
 (a) Hⁿ(f(ℝⁿ ∖ R)) = 0. This is the null-image part of the area formula (Simon Ch. 2, §3): Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.area_image_compl_regularSet_eq_zero (module Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaLipschitz, which the proof file must import), applied to the Lipschitz map f and s := ℝⁿ, gives μHE[dim ℝⁿ](f(ℝⁿ ∖ areaRegularSet f)) = 0; here areaRegularSet f = R by definition and dim ℝⁿ = n (Mathlib finrank_euclideanSpace_fin). [Content: the set of non-differentiability points is Lⁿ-null by Rademacher's theorem, so its image is Hⁿ-null by the Lipschitz image bound used in (b); the image of the critical set {w : f is differentiable at w, Df(w) not injective} is Hⁿ-null by the area formula.]
 (b) Hⁿ(f(Z)) = 0. Each T_p ∖ ⋃_q D_{p,q} is Lⁿ-null (step 3), so Lⁿ(Z) = 0 by countable subadditivity (measure_iUnion_null). The Lipschitz image bound (Simon Ch. 2, 1.8(i); Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn, applied to f restricted to Z) gives Hⁿ(f(Z)) ≤ Kⁿ·Hⁿ(Z), and Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), so Hⁿ(f(Z)) ≤ Kⁿ·Lⁿ(Z) = 0.
 (c) Hence Hⁿ(Y) ≤ Hⁿ(f(ℝⁿ ∖ R)) + Hⁿ(f(Z)) = 0.

6. (Covering.) Let w ∈ ℝⁿ. If w ∉ R, then f(w) ∈ f(ℝⁿ ∖ R) ⊆ Y. If w ∈ R, then w ∈ T_p for some p by step 1. If moreover w ∈ D_{p,q} for some q, then i := Nat.pair p q satisfies (p(i), q(i)) = (p, q), so C_i = D_{p,q} and f(w) ∈ f(C_i). Otherwise w ∈ T_p ∖ ⋃_q D_{p,q} ⊆ Z, so f(w) ∈ f(Z) ⊆ Y. Therefore f(ℝⁿ) ⊆ Y ∪ ⋃_i f(C_i). Together with step 4 (properties of every C_i) and step 5 (Hⁿ(Y) = 0) this proves the theorem.
proof_key_steps: regular_set_lower_lipschitz_cover for the continuous f gives bounded Borel T_p ⊆ R covering R, with lower Lipschitz constants c_p > 0
Bounded sets have finite Lebesgue measure; fderiv ℝ f is Borel (measurable_fderiv) with values in the finite-dimensional space L(ℝⁿ, E)
lusin_compact_exhaustion_of_measurable on each T_p gives compact D_{p,q} ⊆ T_p on which Df is continuous, with Lⁿ(T_p ∖ ⋃_q D_{p,q}) = 0
The pieces C_i := D_{Nat.unpair i} inherit compactness, differentiability with injective derivative, continuity of Df and the lower bound c_p
Y := f(ℝⁿ ∖ R) ∪ f(Z) with Z := ⋃_p (T_p ∖ ⋃_q D_{p,q}): Hⁿ(f(ℝⁿ ∖ R)) = 0 by area_image_compl_regularSet_eq_zero, and Hⁿ(f(Z)) ≤ Kⁿ Lⁿ(Z) = 0
Every f(w) lies in f(ℝⁿ ∖ R), in f(Z) ⊆ Y, or in f(C_{Nat.pair p q})

audit.reason: The exact type matches the prose. Both declared dependencies are used correctly: bounded Borel regular pieces have finite volume, and Lusin applies to the measurable derivative in its finite-dimensional Borel operator space. The compact pieces inherit all required properties. The area lemma handles the nonregular image; the Lipschitz image estimate handles the remaining null set. Reindexing proves the range cover. Applying this child to every original parametrization and taking a Borel null hull proves precisely the selected parent contract, without using the parent or an ancestor theorem.
